transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's nice to meet you too. Um, I’m here because I keep having these nights where I eat an amount of food that honestly scares me. I’ll start with just having some leftovers after grading papers, but then I end up going through boxes of cereal, crackers, peanut butter... and even whatever snacks I packed for my classroom. It's just a lot, and it's happening too often.
After these episodes, do you ever do anything to compensate for what you ate?

Yeah, I do. After one of those nights, I’ll usually tell myself I’m just not allowed to eat breakfast or lunch at school the next day. And then... I’ll stay out on the trail for hours after work, or I'll force myself to do extra yoga. I just keep going even when I’m completely shaky and exhausted. I just feel like I have to make up for it somehow.
How often, on average, do these binge-eating episodes followed by compensation happen?

Um, I'd say for the past few months, it's been pretty constant. There has rarely been a week without at least one night where I eat way more than I meant to. And then, like I said, the next day I try to make up for it by fasting at school or pushing myself through a really long walk or extra yoga. It's happening a lot.
In a typical week, how many times do you have a binge episode followed by compensation?

Well, like I was just saying, for the past few months there has rarely been a week without at least one of these nights. But... if I really think about a typical week, it's honestly a lot more than just once. It's practically every day. 

I'll eat far more than I meant to at night, and then the next day I try to make up for it by not eating anything at school, or pushing myself through another long walk or extra yoga. It's just a constant cycle right now, so it's probably happening six or seven days a week.
Do your weight or body shape strongly affect how you judge yourself as a person?

Yeah, definitely. It really does. Like... if I look even a little softer around my stomach, or if my pants feel tight before a staff meeting, I honestly feel like I’ve failed at everything. It doesn't even matter how well my students are doing, or how prepared I am for my classes. If my body isn't right, none of that other stuff matters and I just feel like a complete failure.

latest_inference.note: The recurrent binge episodes, compensatory fasting/excessive exercise, frequency of 6–7 times weekly, and strong overvaluation of weight/shape support bulimia nervosa and narrow the differential from F50.89.
